project.name: ai-project-guide
project.description: AI Project Guide is a structured methodology and set of guides for AI-assisted software development, giving AI coding tools the context, process, and conventions needed to produce consistently good and verifiable results on complex projects. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: code-review-agent.md
nodes.summary: Specification for an automated code review agent, detailing project-type detection (NextJS, Python, C++, Rust, generic), a four-step review process, output file organization with YAML headers, review criteria, automation triggers (manual, scheduled, CI/CD), configuration options, and success metrics.

nodes.name: task-checker.md
nodes.summary: Claude Code sub-agent definition for a Task Checklist Manager that verifies, updates, and maintains completion status of structured task/checklist files, only marking items complete with explicit confirmation or verifiable evidence.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Claude Code sub-agent YAML frontmatter (name, description, model, color) followed by a natural-language system prompt body.

nodes.name: tester.md
nodes.summary: Claude Code sub-agent definition for a Senior Software Engineer in Test persona, covering unit/integration/e2e test strategy, framework-specific practices (Jest, Vitest, React Testing Library, Playwright), and coverage/quality guidance.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Claude Code sub-agent YAML frontmatter (name, description, model, color) followed by a natural-language system prompt body.

nodes.name: electron.md
nodes.summary: Claude Code auto-attached rule file for Electron desktop apps, covering ESM-vs-CJS module loading, main/renderer process boundaries, and secure preload script patterns via contextBridge. Frontmatter targets electron/**, src/preload/**, and Electron build config files. Likely a generated/derived copy of project-guides/rules/electron.md for Claude Code IDE consumption.

nodes.name: python.md
nodes.summary: Claude Code auto-attached rule file defining Python 3.12+ coding standards: typing conventions, ruff/pyright tooling requirements, exception handling discipline, async/concurrency safety rules, and security practices. Frontmatter targets **/*.py, pyproject.toml, and requirements files. Likely a generated/derived copy of project-guides/rules/python.md for Claude Code IDE consumption.

nodes.name: react.md
nodes.summary: Claude Code auto-attached rule file covering React/Next.js component conventions, state management choices (hooks, Zustand/Jotai, TanStack Query), form handling with react-hook-form/Zod, Tailwind 4 usage, and Radix primitives. Frontmatter targets **/*.tsx, **/*.jsx, and app/**. Likely a generated/derived copy of project-guides/rules/react.md for Claude Code IDE consumption.

nodes.name: sql.md
nodes.summary: Claude Code auto-attached rule file defining SQL/PostgreSQL coding standards covering query formatting, indexing and optimization, naming conventions, security practices, pgvector and TimescaleDB extension-specific patterns, and migration safety. Frontmatter targets **/*.sql and migration files. Likely a generated/derived copy of project-guides/rules/sql.md for Claude Code IDE consumption.

nodes.name: testing.md
nodes.summary: Claude Code auto-attached rule file establishing testing standards across JavaScript/TypeScript (Vitest) and Python (pytest), including test organization, naming conventions, mocking practices, CI integration, and optional Storybook usage. Frontmatter targets test/spec/story files. Likely a generated/derived copy of project-guides/rules/testing.md for Claude Code IDE consumption.

nodes.name: typescript.md
nodes.summary: Claude Code auto-attached rule file establishing strict TypeScript conventions: a hard ban on `any`, discriminated unions over string checks, generics, error-handling patterns, naming conventions, and advanced type patterns (conditional, mapped, template literal types). Frontmatter targets **/*.ts and **/*.tsx. Likely a generated/derived copy of project-guides/rules/typescript.md for Claude Code IDE consumption.
nodes.languageNotes: Extensively uses TypeScript code samples to contrast GOOD/BAD patterns for discriminated unions, generics, const assertions, and mapped/conditional/template-literal types.

nodes.languageNotes: Structured as a fully scripted, copy-pasteable runbook intended for both human and AI consumption, with explicit CLI one-liners to avoid interactive prompts in CI/agent workflows.

nodes.name: guide.app-router.metadata.md
nodes.summary: Developer guide on managing metadata (SEO tags, Open Graph, metadataBase) in Next.js App Router applications, covering static and dynamic metadata patterns, inheritance/composition, and best practices.

nodes.name: guide.markdown.md
nodes.summary: Simplified guide to rendering markdown content in Next.js using gray-matter for frontmatter parsing and remark/remark-html for HTML conversion, avoiding MDX/React-in-Markdown complexity.

nodes.name: guide.troubleshooting-and-upgrading.md
nodes.summary: Troubleshooting reference for common Next.js errors and upgrade issues, including Framer Motion/CSS transform conflicts, async page-prop type incompatibilities from Next.js version upgrades, and codemod-based fixes with before/after code examples.

nodes.name: code-review-agent.md
nodes.summary: Specification for an automated code review agent that scans a project, detects its type (NextJS, Python, C++, Rust, or generic), and produces prioritized review documents and task lists per `.cursor/rules/review.md` guidelines. Defines detection logic, review process steps, output file organization, YAML header conventions, automation triggers, and quality/success metrics.
nodes.languageNotes: Markdown spec document with 45 headings organizing a multi-stage agent workflow (detection, review, generation, reporting).

nodes.name: code-review-config.json
nodes.summary: Configuration data backing the automated code review agent: defines per-project-type detection indicators/directories/extensions (NextJS, Python, C++, Rust, generic), file/directory filters, output formats, quality/resource limits, and integration toggles (git, linting, type-checking, build system).

nodes.name: task-checker.md
nodes.summary: Agent definition for a Task Checklist Manager that verifies and updates checklist/task files, marking items complete only on explicit confirmation or verifiable evidence, and preserving formatting, metadata, and task context. Likely the canonical source template mirrored by the corresponding `.claude/agents` task-checker configuration.

nodes.name: tester.md
nodes.summary: Agent definition for a Senior Software Engineer in Test persona covering unit/integration test strategy, JS/TS testing frameworks (Jest, Vitest, React Testing Library, Playwright), and best practices for maintainable, meaningful test coverage. Likely the canonical source template mirrored by the corresponding `.claude/agents` tester configuration.

nodes.name: guide.ai-project.000-concept.md

nodes.name: guide.ai-project.001-initiative-plan.md

nodes.name: guide.ai-project.003-slice-planning.md
nodes.summary: Phase 3 methodology guide explaining how to break an architecture document into independently deliverable vertical slices, covering slice types, sizing, planning steps, examples, and common pitfalls.

nodes.name: guide.ai-project.004-slice-design.md
nodes.summary: Phase 4 methodology guide for producing detailed low-level slice designs, including a document template, design patterns for feature and migration slices, and a design review checklist.

nodes.name: guide.ai-project.005-task-breakdown.md
nodes.summary: Phase 5 methodology guide describing how to convert a slice design into a granular, checklist-formatted task file, including front matter, test-with-not-test-after strategy, and commit strategy.

nodes.name: guide.ai-project.090-code-review.md
nodes.summary: Supplemental guide defining the code review process, a 12-point review questionnaire covering bugs, security, performance and accessibility, and templates for review documents and resulting task lists.

nodes.name: guide.ai-project.process.md
nodes.summary: Master process guide describing project roles, the full 0-7 phase workflow, phase approval authority, project resource structure, and the living document pattern that underlies the whole AI Project Guide methodology.

nodes.name: guide.ui-development.ai.md
nodes.summary: Short supplemental guide with UI/UX specific guidance covering mockups, wireframes, and color/style handling for AI-assisted development.

nodes.name: prompt.ai-project.system.md

nodes.name: prompt.code-review-crawler.md

nodes.name: general.md
nodes.summary: Language-agnostic core development guidelines covering core principles, code structure, exception handling, source control, lenient parsing practices, and avoidance of hallucination traps in prompts; forms the base ruleset combined with per-technology rules.

nodes.name: git.md
nodes.summary: Canonical Git workflow rules defining branch naming conventions (slice vs planning branches), commit message format with semantic prefixes, and usage guidelines/examples.

nodes.name: python.md
nodes.summary: Canonical Python coding rules covering typing/validation, code style and structure, functions and error handling, modern Python patterns, testing and quality, dependency management, async/performance, concurrency, and security best practices.

nodes.name: react.md
nodes.summary: Canonical React and Next.js coding rules covering component naming/structure, state management, forms, icons, toast notifications, Tailwind usage, Radix primitives, code style, file naming, testing, and builds.

nodes.name: sql.md
nodes.summary: Canonical SQL and PostgreSQL development rules covering query style/formatting, query optimization, PostgreSQL best practices, schema naming, security/safety, pgvector and TimescaleDB specifics, performance monitoring, and migrations.

nodes.name: testing.md
nodes.summary: Canonical testing rules covering general testing philosophy, JavaScript/TypeScript testing frameworks and organization, Python testing frameworks and assertions, best practices, mocking/stubbing, running tests, CI/CD integration, and optional Storybook usage.

nodes.name: typescript.md
nodes.summary: Canonical TypeScript coding rules covering strict mode and the ban on `any`, type design patterns (discriminated unions, unknown, index signatures, interfaces vs type aliases, const assertions), function signatures, generics, error handling, project structure conventions, naming, and advanced type patterns (conditional, mapped, template literal types).
nodes.languageNotes: The most extensive rules file in the set, dedicating substantial space to advanced TypeScript type-system patterns (conditional types, mapped types, template literal types) beyond basic style guidance.

nodes.name: bootstrap.sh
nodes.summary: One-line-curlable install script that sets up a consuming project to use ai-project-guide: creates the project-documents/user/ directory structure, optionally overlays external guides, and adds ai-project-guide as a git submodule with an update-guides wrapper.
nodes.languageNotes: Bash script intended to be piped directly from curl; guards each step with command/state checks (git installed, already-set-up, package.json present) before mutating the filesystem.

nodes.name: migrate-private-to-user.sh
nodes.summary: Idempotent migration script for consumer projects that renames their project-documents/private/ directory to project-documents/user/ and rewrites internal 'private/' path references found in text files.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses git mv for the rename plus scoped sed substitutions with .bak/.tmp backups, only keeping changes that actually differ (cmp -s check) before reporting updated files.

nodes.name: rename-private-to-user-in-repo.sh
nodes.summary: Maintenance script for the ai-project-guide repository itself: rewrites a fixed list of documentation/script files to replace 'private/' path references and ORG_PRIVATE_GUIDES_URL with EXTERNAL_PROJECT_DOC_URL, then renames the private/ directory to user/.
nodes.languageNotes: Distinguishes itself from migrate-private-to-user.sh by targeting the ai-project-guide repo's own source/docs (a hardcoded FILES_TO_UPDATE list) rather than an arbitrary consumer project's private/ directory; verifies it is running inside the ai-project-guide repo via a guide file sentinel check.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Explains the template-stubs directory: two minimal stub scripts (setup-guides.sh, update-guides.sh) meant to be copied into consuming project templates so they can bootstrap and update ai-project-guide without vendoring the full scripts.

nodes.name: prompt.legacy-migration.md
nodes.summary: AI-facing prompt template that instructs an assistant to update a project's private documentation references after migrating ai-project-guide from a git subtree to a git submodule at project-documents/ai-project-guide/ (version 0.9.0).
nodes.languageNotes: Structured as an AI prompt with explicit path-transformation rules, worked examples, and a process checklist rather than human-facing narrative documentation.

nodes.name: setup-guides.sh
nodes.summary: One-line stub script for consuming projects that downloads and executes the canonical bootstrap.sh from the ai-project-guide GitHub repository to perform first-time setup.

nodes.name: update-guides.sh
nodes.summary: Stub script copied into consuming projects to update the ai-project-guide git submodule to the latest main branch, refresh optional external guides, and auto-commit the result.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses set -e for fail-fast behavior and checks EXTERNAL_PROJECT_DOC_URL as an optional environment-driven extension point.

nodes.name: 00-introduction.md
nodes.summary: Entry point for the Electron tool guide series, routing readers to the correct downstream guide and covering process architecture, security best practices, OAuth/authentication, and packaging basics.
nodes.languageNotes: Includes an explicit guide-selection table so AI agents load only the single relevant guide instead of the entire series.

nodes.name: 01-architecture.md
nodes.summary: Architecture guide covering the 'Lichen Pattern', typed IPC contracts, process-agnostic service layers, IPC consolidation patterns, and cross-process state management, plus common anti-patterns.

nodes.name: 02-project-structure.md
nodes.summary: Defines the canonical Electron project layout, file placement rules, a step-by-step checklist for adding a new IPC-backed capability, and testing strategy per layer.

nodes.name: 03-electron-vite.md
nodes.summary: Build and toolchain guide for electron-vite, covering multi-target build configuration, dev vs production differences, electron-builder packaging, TypeScript config, and common build issues.

nodes.name: 04-testing.md
nodes.summary: Testing guide for Electron apps describing the testing pyramid, Vitest setup, unit testing services/components/hooks with mocked IPC, optional IPC integration tests, and what not to test.

nodes.name: 05-decision-guide.md
nodes.summary: Decision framework for choosing Electron versus web-based architectures, including a decision matrix, alternative stacks, a hybrid web-first migration path, and template recommendations.

nodes.name: 01-ios-design.md
nodes.summary: Guide to applying Apple Human Interface Guidelines and Cupertino widgets in a Flutter iOS app, covering the adaptive widget strategy, Material-to-Cupertino widget mapping, navigation/safe-area/typography/action-menu conventions, iPad adaptive layout (breakpoints, split view, slide over), and dark mode. Serves as the design step for both greenfield Flutter iOS apps and Android-to-iOS migrations.

nodes.name: 02-ios-build.md
nodes.summary: Step-by-step guide to configuring Xcode and Apple's toolchain for a Flutter iOS app: opening the correct workspace, setting project identity, signing and capabilities, app icons, launch screen, privacy manifest, building development/ad-hoc/App Store IPAs (including CLI upload for CI/CD), and submitting to TestFlight. Applies to both new apps and Android-to-iOS migrations.

nodes.name: 03-testing.md
nodes.summary: Guide to running unit, widget, and integration tests on a physical iPad for a Flutter iOS app, plus manual checks for orientation, split view/slide over, keyboard, safe areas, dark mode, Apple Pencil/pointer input, and networking permissions, followed by TestFlight beta testing and debugging tools. Completes the design-build-test setup sequence for greenfield and migrated Flutter iOS apps.

nodes.name: introduction.md
nodes.summary: Introductory overview of the manta-templates component and layout system, covering prerequisites, a quickstart, component architecture, layout systems (BentoLayout, GridLayout), essential cards, responsive breakpoints, and the Tailwind CSS v4 styling system.

nodes.name: knowledge.md
nodes.summary: Comprehensive reference for manta-templates covering layout components, card components, container components, hooks, utility functions, theme system, content management, performance tips, troubleshooting, advanced customization, and a migration guide.
nodes.languageNotes: Structured as a component-by-component API reference (49 headings) intended for lookup rather than linear reading, similar to a library's knowledge-base documentation.

nodes.name: setup.md

nodes.name: introduction.md

nodes.name: radix-colors-quick-reference.md

nodes.name: radix-theming-guide.md

nodes.languageNotes: Documents a semantic color layering pattern (raw palette variables mapped to semantic role variables mapped to component variants) that decouples component styling from any specific palette, enabling runtime theme switching via CSS custom properties and data attributes.

nodes.name: introduction.md
nodes.summary: Tailwind CSS v4 installation and setup guide covering framework-specific instructions for Next.js, Vite, Astro, and SvelteKit, plus a summary of v4 utility class changes and browser support.

nodes.name: guide.tailwindcss.v4.md
nodes.summary: Explains the key changes in Tailwind CSS v4, including a minimal CSS config example and a v3-vs-v4 comparison table, to guide migration and setup.

nodes.name: guide.themes.v4.md
nodes.summary: Theming guide for Tailwind CSS v4 covering formatted color tokens via `@theme`, dark mode and custom theme support, a paste-ready `globals.css` example, and a pre-commit migration checklist.

nodes.name: guide.syntax-highlighting.v4.md
nodes.summary: Guide on implementing syntax highlighting in a Tailwind CSS v4 app using Shiki/rehype-shiki and rehype-pretty-code, comparing approaches for MDX and plain Markdown pipelines.

nodes.name: introduction.md
nodes.summary: Entry-point introduction to the Three.js tool guide, explaining what Three.js is, who should use the guide, prerequisites, and the layout of the other guides in the folder (setup, overview, WebGPU, lighting, deployment).

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with readme.md, the public front door of the repository. It introduces ai-project-guide as a phase-based methodology that gives AI coding tools the context, process, and conventions they need to work reliably on complex projects. The README also previews the installation model (a bootstrap script plus a git submodule) and points to Context Forge as the MCP server that makes the methodology transparent to use — everything else in this tour fills in the details it sketches.

tour.title: The Contracts Behind the README
tour.description: Two root documents turn the README's promises into enforceable rules. directory-structure.md is the canonical contract for where every guide, snippet, and asset must live, including a decision matrix for placing new documents. file-naming-conventions.md defines the YAML frontmatter every document must carry and the per-doctype schemas referenced throughout the rest of the repository — it has the highest fan-in of any node in the graph, meaning nearly everything downstream depends on its definitions.

tour.title: The Master Process Guide
tour.description: project-guides/readme.md is the navigation index for the methodology's core: it links every workflow phase to its primary guide and lists supplemental guides, prompts, agents, and rules. From there, guide.ai-project.process.md is the master document describing project roles, the full 0-7 phase workflow, phase approval authority, and the 'living document' pattern that underlies the entire system. This is the conceptual heart of ai-project-guide — everything else exists to support this process.

tour.title: Walking the Phases: Concept to Slices
tour.description: The process guide fans out into individual phase guides, each owning one step of the pipeline: guide.ai-project.000-concept.md captures the initial problem statement and solution direction, guide.ai-project.001-initiative-plan.md decomposes a concept into named initiatives, and guide.ai-project.003-slice-planning.md breaks an architecture into independently deliverable vertical slices. These three guides form a tightly coupled cluster in the dependency graph — they cross-reference each other constantly because each phase's output is the next phase's input.

tour.title: Design, Tasks, and Prompts to Drive Them
tour.description: guide.ai-project.004-slice-design.md turns a slice into a detailed low-level design, and guide.ai-project.005-task-breakdown.md converts that design into a granular, checklist-formatted task file ready for implementation. prompt.ai-project.system.md is the master library of parameterized prompt templates that actually drives an AI agent through every one of these phases — it has one of the highest fan-out counts in the graph because it links back to nearly every phase guide it operationalizes.

tour.title: Per-Technology Rules and Sub-Agents
tour.description: Below the phase workflow sits project-guides/rules/general.md, a language-agnostic base ruleset covering core principles, code structure, and exception handling. It fans out to per-technology rule files (Python, React, TypeScript, SQL, testing, git, Dart, Flutter) that layer technology-specific conventions on top. Alongside the rules, project-guides/agents/code-review-agent.md defines an automated review sub-agent, paired with its own JSON configuration describing per-project-type detection logic — together they show how the methodology extends from documentation into agent behavior.
tour.languageLesson: This repository practices what it teaches: general.md is the DRY base, and each technology file only adds what's different, mirroring the 'don't duplicate logic' principle it documents for actual codebases.

tour.title: From Canonical Rules to IDE Rules
tour.description: scripts/setup-ide is the highest fan-out node in the entire graph — it reads every rules, agent, and skill file under project-guides/ and compiles them into the format each AI coding tool expects (Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot). The .claude/rules/typescript.md file is a generated-from copy of project-guides/rules/typescript.md, produced by this exact script. This is the mechanism that makes the methodology 'mostly transparent,' as the README puts it: authors write once in project-guides/, and setup-ide propagates it to whichever IDE a developer uses.
tour.languageLesson: Bash scripts like this one define single-purpose functions (find_project_root, validate_frontmatter, compile_claude_rules) and chain them from one main() dispatcher — a pattern worth recognizing when reading any nontrivial shell tooling.

tour.title: Bootstrapping a Consumer Project
tour.description: scripts/bootstrap.sh is the install-time counterpart to setup-ide: it is the one-line-curlable script that sets up a brand-new consuming project, creating the project-documents/user/ directory structure and adding ai-project-guide as a git submodule. The .gitmodules config is what that submodule registration actually produces — pointing project-documents/ai-project-guide/ at this repository on GitHub. Together they explain how a project pulls this methodology in without vendoring or copying it wholesale.
tour.languageLesson: Git submodules pin a consuming project to a specific commit of an external repository, letting update-guides.sh later fast-forward that pin independently of the host project's own history.

tour.title: Tool and Framework Guides
tour.description: Beyond the core methodology, the repository ships an entire library of per-tool developer guides. The Electron guide series is the graph's most tightly-coupled cluster: 00-introduction.md routes readers to 01-architecture.md (covering typed IPC contracts and process boundaries), 02-project-structure.md, 03-electron-vite.md, and 04-testing.md, each linking forward to the next in sequence. This 'introduction routes to numbered guides' pattern repeats across Three.js, Flutter-iOS, Radix, and Tailwind — it's the standard shape for any multi-document tool guide in this repository.

tour.title: Domain Guides and the Guide-on-Guides
tour.description: domain-guides/introduction.md anchors a smaller section covering cross-cutting domain knowledge like 2D game development platform choice. More importantly, domain-guides/guide-development/guide.guide-creation.md is the meta-guide that specifies the required file set, frontmatter schema, and writing-style checklist for authoring any new tool or domain guide in this repository — it is effectively the constitution that produced every guide seen in Step 9.

tour.title: Self-Hosted: The Methodology Used on Itself
tour.description: The user/ directory is where this repository applies its own methodology to manage its maintenance work — the layer the script analysis calls 'self-hosted project data.' user/architecture/110-arch.schema-and-phases-update.md is a real architecture document proposing canonical YAML schemas and phase restructuring, which decomposes into user/architecture/110-slices.schema-and-phases-update.md, a slice plan covering three concrete slices. This is the exact Concept-to-Architecture-to-Slice-Plan flow from Steps 3-5, now visible as lived history rather than abstract instruction.

tour.title: From Slice to Tasks: Closing the Loop
tour.description: user/slices/111-slice.phase-renumbering-and-initiative-plan.md is one of the concrete slices spawned by Step 11's slice plan, restructuring phase numbering and introducing the Initiative Plan phase you saw in Step 4. It references user/tasks/111-tasks.phase-renumbering-and-initiative-plan.md, the granular checklist-formatted task breakdown that actually implemented it — the same slice-to-task relationship guide.ai-project.005-task-breakdown.md (Step 5) describes in the abstract, now completed and marked done.

tour.title: Ongoing Maintenance and Change History
tour.description: user/tasks/950-tasks.maintenance.md is the repository's living, centralized tech-debt and maintenance checklist, referencing historical migration inventories and completion reports. At the root level, CHANGELOG.md and DEVLOG.md provide the project-wide chronological record: the changelog tracks released versions, while the append-only devlog captures day-to-day decisions and open issues. Together they show how this project tracks its own evolution using the same document conventions it prescribes for consumers.
